subject.title: [Architecture] Migration of transient plugin state to Agent-Scoped SQLite cache tables

question: Should OpenClaw expose agent-scoped persistent cache storage to third-party plugins, and if so, under which capability and agent-isolation rules?
rationale: The current API is deliberately plugin-global and trusted-only; changing that contract affects third-party permissions, agent data isolation, database lifecycle ownership, and the shipped Plugin SDK surface.

options.title: Design a constrained agent store
options.body: Add a capability-gated SDK abstraction scoped by plugin and agent identity, with quotas, TTL cleanup, lifecycle rules, and isolation tests before exposing it externally.

options.title: Keep plugin-global storage
options.body: Retain the existing trusted-only keyed store and require plugins to encode agent identity within their namespace when that ownership model is acceptable.

options.title: Defer third-party persistence
options.body: Keep the external API unavailable until the broader third-party plugin permissions model is settled.

recommendation.title: Design a constrained agent store
recommendation.body: Add a capability-gated SDK abstraction scoped by plugin and agent identity, with quotas, TTL cleanup, lifecycle rules, and isolation tests before exposing it externally.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing plugin-state runtime is the central contract that would need to own or delegate this new capability.
